favourite.heading: Why Ole Miss can pull away
bullets: Ole Miss is the better football team by 30.2 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 86% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+30.2 pts).
Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 6.6 points to Ole Miss (+6.6 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Ole Miss by 5.6 points: ball control vs front disruption (+5.6 pts).
Playing at Ole Miss is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Charlotte can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 +22.4 to p90 +67.4 for Ole Miss, so a projection of +46.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
60% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
